title: Slack AI: privacy-first generative AI architecture
problem: Deliver generative AI features while keeping customer data inside the trust boundary and honouring existing compliance commitments.
depth: Detailed on security and hosting decisions; no quality or latency metrics
technologies_stated: Closed-source LLMs hosted in an AWS escrow VPC
facts: Four principles: customer data stays in the trust boundary, no training on customer data, AI only shows what the user can already see, and enterprise security and compliance still apply.
Closed-source models run in an escrow VPC on AWS so the model provider has no access to customer data.
Slack chose off-the-shelf models with RAG over fine-tuning on customer data because it could not guarantee sufficient protections.
Retrieval uses the requesting user's access control lists and existing display libraries; output is visible only to the requester.
Outputs are ephemeral and not written to disk; stored data follows a least-data principle and existing key management and residency infrastructure.
If a source message is removed by DLP, derived summaries are invalidated.
interpretations: Reusing existing authorisation code paths for retrieval is a strong pattern: the AI layer inherits, rather than reimplements, access control.
unknown: Technical detail of the escrow VPC
Prompt construction and evaluation (deferred by the authors)

decisions.selected: Provider models inside an escrow VPC
decisions.alternatives: Hosted provider API; self-hosted open model; vendor-managed private deployment
decisions.reasoning: Source documents data-ownership requirement and that vendors generally do not ship closed models for self-hosting.
Source states it could not guarantee strong enough protection if training on customer data.
Source states AI must show only what the user can already see.

review_exercise: Derived summaries are invalidated when a source message is deleted. Identify two other places an AI system might retain derivatives of deleted data and how to detect them.
lessons: Start from non-negotiable data principles and derive hosting choices from them.
Inherit authorisation from the system of record.
adaptation: Maps directly to SAP CX client conversations about data residency and no-training terms with Generative AI Hub. Independent analysis.
